title: Antagonist binding actively disrupts interleukin-1 receptor dynamics to block co-receptor recruitment
authors: Chandran Nithin; Ayomide Fasemire; Sebastian Kmiecik
one_liner_zh: 该文用MD和CABS-flex研究IL1R1受体-配体动态构象变化，虽涉及蛋白-蛋白互作与动态机制，但对象为受体-配体而非蛋白质-DNA互作，方法可迁移性有限，仅边缘相关。
abstract: The interleukin-1 receptor type 1 (IL1R1) is a central regulator of inflammatory signaling and functions as a molecular switch, yet it remains unclear how agonists and antagonists that bind the same primary site produce opposite signaling outcomes. Available structural data define inactive and active endpoint conformations but do not explain how antagonist binding dynamically prevents co-receptor recruitment. Here, we combine all-atom molecular dynamics simulations with multiscale flexibility modeling using CABS-flex to systematically compare the intrinsic dynamics of IL1R1 across its unbound, agonist-bound, antagonist-bound, and co-receptor–bound states. Although both agonists and antagonists engage the same conserved interface on the D1/D2 domains, they induce fundamentally different dynamic responses in the receptor. Agonist binding progressively stabilizes interdomain coupling and promotes a stepwise transition toward a signaling-competent conformation. In contrast, antagonist binding selectively increases flexibility of the distal D3 domain, particularly at the co-receptor binding interface, thereby preventing progression along the activation pathway. Importantly, the interaction patterns and dynamic signatures observed in the simulations are consistent with experimentally identified binding determinants, mutational data, and structural features associated with receptor activation and inhibition. These results demonstrate that IL1R1 antagonism is an active, allosteric, dynamics-driven process rather than a simple failure to stabilize an active conformation. Together, this work provides a mechanistic framework that reconciles existing structural and functional observations and highlights receptor dynamics as a key determinant of signaling control in the interleukin-1 system.
abstract_zh: 白细胞介素-1受体1型（IL1R1）是炎症信号传导的核心调节因子，并作为分子开关发挥作用，然而，结合相同初级位点的激动剂和拮抗剂如何产生相反的信号结果仍不清楚。现有结构数据定义了非活性和活性终点构象，但未解释拮抗剂结合如何动态阻止共受体招募。在此，我们结合全原子分子动力学（molecular dynamics）模拟与使用CABS-flex的多尺度柔性建模，系统比较IL1R1在未结合、激动剂结合、拮抗剂结合及共受体结合状态下的内在动力学。尽管激动剂和拮抗剂均与D1/D2结构域上相同的保守界面结合，但它们在受体中诱导根本不同的动态响应。激动剂结合逐步稳定结构域间耦合，并促进向信号活性构象的阶梯式转变。相反，拮抗剂结合选择性地增加远端D3结构域的柔性，特别是在共受体结合界面处，从而阻止沿激活途径的进展。重要的是，模拟中观察到的相互作用模式和动态特征与实验确定的结合决定因素、突变数据及与受体激活和抑制相关的结构特征一致。这些结果表明，IL1R1拮抗作用是一个主动的、别构的、动力学驱动的过程，而非简单未能稳定活性构象。综合来看，这项工作提供了一个机制框架，调和了现有结构和功能观察，并强调受体动力学是白细胞介素-1系统中信号控制的关键决定因素。
